title: Equality of the Jellium and the Uniform Electron Gas Energies
abstract: Jellium, a system of electrons in a uniform neutralizing background, and the uniform electron gas (UEG), a system of electrons with constant density and no background, are two standard models of the electron gas. We prove that the ground-state energy per unit volume of Jellium, as defined by Lieb and Narnhofer, coincides with the UEG energy defined by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer, i.e. \[ e^\hbar_{\rm Jel}(ρ_0)=e^\hbar_{\rm UEG}(ρ_0). \] This equality was previously established in the classical case by Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer and independently by Cotar and Petrache.
summary: This paper proves the mathematical equality between the ground-state energy of the Jellium model and the Uniform Electron Gas (UEG) model for interacting electrons. By establishing two opposing inequalities, the authors confirm that the energy calculated using a background potential matches the energy calculated using a pure density functional approach. This is a major theoretical result confirming consistency across different models of electron correlation.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously prove the equality between the ground-state energy per unit volume calculated for the Jellium model and the Uniform Electron Gas (UEG) model in the quantum mechanical limit.
main_result: The core result is the mathematical proof that the ground-state energy per unit volume for Jellium, $e\hbar_{	ext{Jel}}(ho_0)$, exactly equals the energy for the UEG, $e\hbar_{	ext{UEG}}(ho_0)$.
method: The proof strategy involves establishing two inequalities ($e_{	ext{Jel}} \le e_{	ext{UEG}}$ and $e_{	ext{UEG}} \le e_{	ext{Jel}}$) by comparing energy functionals derived from different physical definitions (canonical vs. grand-canonical).
model_or_system: The study concerns interacting electrons modeled by two systems: Jellium (electrons in a uniform neutralizing background) and the UEG (electrons with constant density and no background). The Hamiltonian involves kinetic energy and electron-electron/electron-background interactions.
key_observables: Ground-state energy per unit volume ($e\hbar_{	ext{Jel}}(ho_0)$ and $e\hbar_{	ext{UEG}}(ho_0)$), and the energy functional $J$.
important_parameters: Electron density ($ho_0$), and the quantum parameter $\hbar$.
main_assumptions: The Jellium energy uses a thermodynamic limit with specific 'LN-admissible' boundary conditions, while the UEG energy uses a grand-canonical approach with density smoothing.
figures_summary: Figure 1 sketches the equality of the two energy functions versus density. Figure 2 illustrates the boundary layers used in the admissibility conditions for the Jellium model.
paper_structure: The paper builds the proof by first establishing the necessary mathematical frameworks for both energy definitions, then proving the two required inequalities ($e_{	ext{Jel}} \le e_{	ext{UEG}}$ and $e_{	ext{UEG}} \le e_{	ext{Jel}}$) through detailed energy bounding and construction arguments.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical confirmation of a fundamental physical identity in condensed matter theory, linking two seemingly distinct theoretical models of electron interactions.
